function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Reconstruct the public evidence chain for the 2023 3CX DesktopApp software supply-chain compromise using only evidence available from benchmark tools and citing exclusively the exact source IDs those tools provide. Produce a detailed, source-ID-grounded research memo covering: (1) the earliest publicly evidenced access, intrusion, or malicious artifact and how the compromise was initially initiated, including all uncertainty about origin; (2) how the compromise propagated into or through 3CX software-development, build, code-signing, packaging, release, update, or distribution systems; (3) how malicious 3CX DesktopApp builds or updates were delivered, including affected platforms/components, observed behavior, and publicly evidenced impact; and (4) attribution to a threat-activity cluster, distinguishing directly confirmed facts from vendor, government, researcher, or other assessments, and identifying allegations, competing attributions, contradictions, and unresolved uncertainty. Search and use authoritative primary sources where available (3CX, Mandiant, CrowdStrike, Sophos, SentinelOne, Kaspersky, Microsoft, CISA or other government advisories, incident reports, and relevant technical analyses). Preserve source IDs exactly as returned by the benchmark tools; do not invent entity IDs, relationship names, facts, or citations. Explicitly separate evidence from inference and note when sources disagree or only allege a conclusion. Return a structured memo that can be converted into a final Markdown report with the user-required arrays: findings (question, answer, supporting_entities, source_references), claims (claim, source_references), reasoning_steps (id, conclusion, premise_entities, premise_relations), and contradictions (contradiction_id, description, source_references)."}
function.name: ConductResearch
